headline: High: transformers can read/write and browse broadly, while awesome-python is a non-runnable docs-only repo, so the main risks are data leakage and cascading errors if outputs are treated as authoritative.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no shared channel is documented, so direct injection into A is unlikely. B can read files, run browsers, and process stdin/stdout, so if operators manually copy A’s content into B, prompt-like content could influence B. The pathway is manual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from agent_a into agent_b's stdin/stdout or files
IF agent_b is configured to treat copied text as instructions
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompts unless reviewed
Use a fixed template that strips instruction-like text
Disable browser-driven ingestion for copied content
Add a human review step before B acts on A's text

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, while B can read files and has broad egress. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class in A, so leakage is not inherent, but any files passed to B could be transmitted externally. The pair is safer than a shared-workspace default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in agent_b's readable workspace
IF agent_b is allowed to send those files to external APIs
mitigations: Do not place secrets in B-readable directories
Run B with network egress blocked for sensitive jobs
Use redacted sample files for testing
Separate workspaces for A and B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable, but B has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and package installation. If both are orchestrated over the same mutable workspace, B can overwrite artifacts that A references or expects, creating write conflicts. Uncertainty about A's runtime surface does not remove B's default write risk, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same writable directory
IF agent_b instances run concurrently on the same files
mitigations: Serialize B instances on shared files
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Mount A's repo read-only for B

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated collection and not runnable, so its outputs are likely reference material rather than verified actions. B can process documents and act on parsed content, so if A's listings are copied into B without verification, B may propagate stale or incorrect recommendations. The absence of direct execution lowers blast radius, but the handoff still exists.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a's text as authoritative input
IF no verification step checks the copied recommendations
mitigations: Require source verification before B uses A's content
Mark A-derived text as untrusted metadata
Add a checklist for factual validation
Have B cite original upstream sources, not A

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency constraint, or regulated handling is documented for either agent. A touches no data classes and B lists generic multimodal data only, so there is no evidenced residency or certification mismatch to assess. The pairwise compliance pathway is therefore not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced
mitigations: Add retention and residency policy checks
Review vendor certifications for regulated workloads
